## Result

- Skill: delivery-review.
- Review status: approved.
- Package member: exact registered primary plan docs/plans/2026-09-10-release-validation-integration.md.
- Upstream: current Design Review design-review-r2; unchanged adopted CLI current-work discovery and Workflow scoped retirement governance.
- Review ID and round: delivery-review-r5, round 5.
- Traceability: adequate complete M1 allocation, including bounded archival inventory/current-catalog reconciliation.
- Material findings: none new; original rvi-delivery-f1 remains resolved.
- Correction targets and Delivery blockers: none.
- Recording: targeted v2 review and prior applicability update; validation follows save.
- Next owner: route for existing M1 implementation and independent assessment.
- Limits: no implementation approval, complete CI success, Verify, PR or publication readiness.

## Independent assessment

I authored none of this plan, models, tests or implementation. Read the complete revised primary plan and its bounded delta, current exact approved Design members, Workflow scoped retirement table (WF-SR-10 and mapped R14/R17-R20/R22-R25), and actual archival ledger/current selector/test consumers. Design r2 Release and guidance members remain byte-identical; its old contextual plan identity is allocation history, not another normative Design member. This review establishes the newly registered plan. Preserve prior r4 judgment with stale applicability.

The added M1 step 5 restores an already-selected current/archival distinction. Workflow forbids rewriting the earlier archival retirement ledger and requires affected consumers to reflect exact current retirement dispositions. The current selector owns record_retirement.regression, whereas the old ledger contains compact_contract.canonical. The two currently failing inventory assertions compare that historical catalog directly to today's catalog. Neither restoring retired behavior nor silently rewriting the old ledger is justified.

The plan selects precisely one catalog-slot disposition in the test comparison, requires retired absence/current presence and exact coverage plus unique ownership for all remaining entries, and preserves structural and negative cases. This is not a claim that the current retirement check reproduces old compact-contract behavior. The separate actual node record-retirement suite proves current support/rejection. Its invocation is already the current selector check's command, so proof is executable without a new framework or runtime policy. The historical ledger remains inspected evidence with unchanged bytes and judgments. No production catalog change, broad ledger exemption, generic ignored-ID list or test deletion is allocated.

This dependency fits existing M1 ordinary-main compatibility scope: the direct main graph must run its required governance checks after prepared release checks. Both inventory validation and unique ownership must consume the same explicit disposition without masking any other difference. Actual implementation review must verify the mapping cannot accept unknown/missing/duplicate checks and must verify historical bytes remain unchanged. The existing failed observation is retained; the plan's focused Python ledger suite plus separate current retirement command provide proportional proof before the complete main graph.

## Whole-plan sequencing and proof

All other reviewed M1 allocations remain intact: real isolated exact-source candidate preparation shared by selected PR and direct main; all direct main gates and execution order; actual packed runtime overlay; exact checked identity and original source preservation; malformed/pending/current/historical distinction; current dynamic versus fixed historical fixtures; CI-only nonpublication and hosted fresh-candidate public eligibility. No existing failure can become a fallback success. Prior r4 discovery reasoning remains applicable because its governing CLI table and allocated safe classification, explicit/current invalid IDs, mixed/malformed stores, reserved residue and unsafe-path negatives remain unchanged.

The complete plan requires focused release/selector/discovery/ledger/current-retirement checks, then actual ci.sh --mode pr and --mode main on the same newly committed final source and recorded base/head, with direct dispatch/failure regressions. A PR partial pass or discovery-only/main precheck does not establish the entire main graph. Earlier interrupted and failed runs remain such; author-reported focused successes are useful implementation evidence but are not converted into a Delivery correctness judgment. Existing model/prose/record validation remains required.

One M1 remains proportionate for this coherent integration correction. Independent M1 review and a separate fresh final whole-change Code Review precede distinct Verify. No work reinitialization, historical migration, new Design behavior, gate waiver, external-service publication or expansion to unrelated cleanup is selected. Recovery preserves archival evidence and existing release safeguards. npm setup and final release approval remain external prerequisites.

## Checks and handoff

Performed exact subject inspection, complete plan read, current Design member freshness checks, scoped Workflow/CLI contract and actual inventory/catalog consumer inspection, authoritative context refresh and targeted recording. This Delivery review did not run runtime tests or edit engineering, plans, models, activity or work. Scoped record-store validation and diff checks follow persistence. Return to route for the approved bounded correction; final proof remains outstanding.
independence_basis: Independent original nonauthor assessed complete revised plan and existing Workflow/CLI retirement/discovery owners; no engineering or authoring edits.
